label: caiso netrev margin keeper
definition: CAISO net-revenue margin KEEPER: structurally-correct fuel-invariant gas offer form (rule 1/11 — replaces the multiplicative markup form; single delta gas_offer_margin=true, anchor 4.7964). C3b dip is the removal of the multiplicative form's masking of the ledgered scarcity/import mid-tail (caiso-107/109/111), not an offer-form defect.
market_story: gas_cc / gas_ct / gas_st: real CAISO gas bidders express their above-cost offer as a net-revenue TARGET in $/MWh (start/no-load recovery, competitive reach, the soft-cap scarcity wall), NOT as a fixed multiple of the fuel bill. The net-revenue margin form encodes exactly this: each band's physical burn (the measured CAMPD marginal heat rate) tracks delivered gas, while the above-physical markup is a gas-INVARIANT $/MWh margin anchored at the 2023-25 delivered-gas mean. So a CC's offer/mc compresses toward 1 as gas rises (the $-margin is a shrinking fraction of a bigger fuel bill) and firms at cheap gas — the observed fuel-invariant bidding the old multiplicative form could not reproduce (it ballooned the markup at high gas). The class energy and merit order are unchanged at the anchor; only the gas-elasticity of the offer above cost changes, which is the structurally-correct behavior.
